summary: Verified fix for CI/CD Docker build failure caused by `emergentintegrations==0.2.2` (and `litellm @ <url>#sha256`) living inside backend/requirements.txt where pip could not resolve them without the private --extra-index-url. Confirmed both lines are removed from /app/backend/requirements.txt. Reproduced the Dockerfile install sequence inside a FRESH venv (python3 -m venv /tmp/ci_venv) on the container (python3.11 since python3.13 is only present inside the Docker image). Steps run: (1) `pip install --upgrade pip` OK, (2) `pip install --dry-run -r /app/backend/requirements.txt` resolved all 156 pins with exit 0 (no mention of emergentintegrations/litellm — proves the failing line is gone), (3) `pip install emergentintegrations==0.2.2 --extra-index-url https://d33sy5i8bnduwe.cloudfront.net/simple/` succeeded and transitively pulled litellm-1.80.0, (4) `pip check` -> No broken requirements found, (5) `python -c 'import emergentintegrations, litellm'` OK. Also verified local running backend remains healthy: GET http://localhost:8001/api/ -> 200 {"message":"AzoApp Home Service Platform API","status":"ok"}. Docker binary not available in container so `docker build /app/backend` could not be executed, but the exact RUN command on lines 26-29 of the Dockerfile was reproduced step-by-step with success. Dockerfile unchanged as intended.
critical_code_review_comments: Dockerfile pins emergentintegrations==0.2.2 inline; consider moving to a dedicated requirements-emergent.txt so CI/CD and local devs share a single source of truth and version bumps don't require editing the Dockerfile.
Dockerfile uses python:3.13-slim while supervisor runs python3.11 locally — pin a single interpreter version or test both to avoid wheel-availability surprises (we got lucky on the dry-run).
context_for_next_testing_agent: CI/CD build issue fixed. requirements.txt is clean of emergentintegrations and litellm url lines. Dockerfile lines 26-29 do the right thing (requirements first, then emergentintegrations via --extra-index-url). Docker CLI is not installed in this preview container, so a true `docker build` cannot be executed here — the only remaining risk is Python 3.13 wheel availability, which looks fine based on dry-run resolution on 3.11.
rca of the issue: Root cause: requirements.txt declared `emergentintegrations==0.2.2` and a direct-URL `litellm @ <cloudfront>#sha256=...` pin. The default PyPI index has no emergentintegrations package, and pip install -r requirements.txt in the Dockerfile does not pass --extra-index-url, so resolution failed with 'Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement emergentintegrations==0.2.2'. Mitigation: removed both lines from requirements.txt; Dockerfile already installs emergentintegrations==0.2.2 separately with --extra-index-url https://d33sy5i8bnduwe.cloudfront.net/simple/, which also pulls litellm transitively. Reproduction (success): `python3 -m venv /tmp/ci_venv && /tmp/ci_venv/bin/pip install --upgrade pip && /tmp/ci_venv/bin/pip install --dry-run -r /app/backend/requirements.txt && /tmp/ci_venv/bin/pip install emergentintegrations==0.2.2 --extra-index-url https://d33sy5i8bnduwe.cloudfront.net/simple/ && /tmp/ci_venv/bin/pip check` -> all exit 0.
